title: Feature loop run review actions
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>As

commits.summary: JBMC's phases are exclusive: post-processing counted once, overcounts flagged (verification pending)
commits.body:
Phase 1a of engine-priorities.md, in the jbmc stream. CBMC 6.11.0's 'Runtime Solver' times a whole solver call, including the 'Runtime Post-process' reported from inside it. lib/src/phases.rs counted both, so JBMC's phases added up past the run, for example 22.0 s of phases in 15.9 s on held/reverse in job 20261106-102624. It now reads the timers per solver call. Post-processing counts as encoding, and the rest of the call as solving. A call that never reached the SAT solver (out of memory while post-processing) counts entirely as encoding. A run cut off mid-call still gives the rest of its time to the phase it was in.

Phases::excess flags a run whose named phases add up past its seconds by more than 1% plus 5 ms. The excess is recorded as phases_excess on each checker run, never scaled to fit. lib/benchmark/run.py carries it as phasesExcess and leaves such runs out of the 'Where the time goes' tables, naming them below. The recorded RESULTS.md (job -102624) stands as written, and its README now says its JBMC shares overcount.

Verified against real JBMC 6.11.0 output captured on cvm, kept as fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-phases/ (README says how each was made): held/prefix-sums proved, the same cut off by a 1.9 s budget, held/reverse out of memory at 700 MiB, and a run with two solver calls. The tests check each phase against JBMC's own Runtime figures, that the phases add up to the run, and that the old double count is flagged. The Rust lib (150), integration (63) and skill tests pass, as do lib/benchmark/test_run.py's 19. conformance.rs's the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_on_the_tools_own_checker fails on cvm with 12 disagreements. Its messages point to the contract library's records being for JDK 25.0.4.1 while cvm has 25.0.5, not to this change; this is recorded under Progress for the reconcile loop.

Job 20261106-192959 fetches CBMC's source at the cbmc-6.11.0 tag (a network fetch, inside the job) and checks that the timers nest as the fixtures show.

commits.summary: Every result names its SAT solver, version and configuration, on both engines
commits.body: Phase 1b of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md (the engines-jbmc stream). The JSON's stated.checker now carries sat: the solver, its version, its source and its configuration (Sat in lib/src/statement.rs). The own checker's is CaDiCaL 1.9.5 as the cadical crate 0.1.16 bundles it (the crate's version read from Cargo.lock), with default options, incremental, and the deadline through the terminate callback. JBMC's is the solver the adapter asks for, with the options every JBMC run passes (jbmc::standing_options, which now also builds the command line) and the version of the CaDiCaL linked into the executable, read from its signature without running JBMC: cadical-3.0.0 in JBMC 6.11.0. An executable with no CaDiCaL is recorded with JBMC's default solver, which the unknown-solver retry falls back to. lib/benchmark/run.py keeps each run's sat and lists each engine's solvers in results.json's environment.sat; RESULTS.md names them, and the recorded job -102624 renders as before.

commits.summary: Propose this session's mangled C++ symbol names for the allow list; note the resubmitted CBMC source job

commits.summary: JBMC's staging policy is an option: staged, full range alone, or one tight stage first
commits.body:
Step 2a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. `--jbmc-staging` on `equivalence` and `prove` picks which of JBMC's interval stages run before the full range (`deadline::Staging`). `staged` is today's search and stays the default until the 2b job decides. `full-range` runs the full range alone and shrinks its counterexample in the interpreter. `tight` runs the first stage that leaves out an input on at most a fortieth of the check, then the full range. The deadline, bounds, models, preflights, gap rules and stop rule are the same under each, and the own checker's stages and --confirm don't follow the policy. A JBMC verdict records the policy as search.staging.

Verified with unit tests in deadline.rs for each policy's stages and budgets, and an end-to-end test in conformance.rs (added) against a stand-in JBMC answering stage by stage. It checks the stages and budgets on property and regression checks, a slow first stage handing on, and violations from the wide stage and the full range, both shrunk to the same witness. Mutating equivalence to ignore the option fails it. Lib 155, integration 63 and skill tests pass. Conformance fails only as before: 12 JDK 25.0.5 disagreements in the corpus test, recorded in Progress. Shared files are named under Progress. Noted for 2c: under --engine auto, a staged fallback whose two preliminary stages time out leaves the full range no time.

commits.summary: Record that CBMC 6.11.0's source nests Runtime Post-process inside Runtime Solver, as phases.rs assumes
commits.body: Job 20261106-194328, the resubmitted source check for step 1a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md, passed in the default workspace. run_property_decider times property_decider.solve() as Runtime Solver (bmc_util.cpp:393-400). dec_solve, inside it, runs finish_eager_conversion once, guarded by post_processing_done, and prints Runtime Post-process (prop_conv_solver.cpp:449-461). That is the nesting lib/src/phases.rs counts once. Only the Progress note in the stream brief changes.

commits.summary: The benchmark runs JBMC under each staging policy and compares them, proofs and counterexamples apart (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 2b of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. lib/benchmark/run.py takes --jbmc-staging, a list of JBMC's staging policies (staged, full-range, tight, from step 2a), and makes every jbmc run once per policy. An auto run is made under the first policy, and again under the others only where the own checker gave no verdict and JBMC's fallback ran. Each run records its policy, auto's fallback, and its witness's size after lib/src/shrink.rs and as the engine found it (array elements, largest magnitude). The corpus's tables, 'Where the time goes' among them, stay over the first policy. A new RESULTS.md section compares the others with it per engine and mode, proofs and counterexamples apart: verdicts, seconds, class changes, larger witnesses, and auto fallbacks whose full range got under a second. Results and the page name the pipeline job and commit they come from.

Verified: test_run.py passes (26 tests, 5 new). Job 20261106-102624's results.json still renders to the committed RESULTS.md byte for byte. A smoke run of group 2 under strict on the own checker and auto, with a stub for JBMC, ran each auto case once, since none fell back. Job 20261106-201041 runs the whole corpus (groups 1-4) on native, jbmc and auto under strict, assume and advised, with all three policies; step 2c decides JBMC's default from it.

The brief's 2b asks for the JBMC cases under all three policies; this job also measures auto's fallback under them, since 2c's default covers the fallback too.

commits.summary: JBMC lets a runtime exception past its handler in two shapes: the preflight names them and refuses a JBMC proof through one (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 3 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. JBMC's counterexamples to conformance/caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 (n=0) did not reproduce because JBMC 6.11.0 lets a runtime exception past the handler that catches it on the JVM, so the exception escapes the method. It is not the models, the harness, or the trace reading. There are two shapes, found by running JBMC (milliseconds) on the cases and on variants of them, written up in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/README.md. (1) A JBMC defect: for 'try { return 10 / n; } catch (ArithmeticException e)', javac ends the handler's range before ireturn, and JBMC emits the quotient, with the check --throw-runtime-exceptions adds, at the ireturn, after its pop_catch. The same holds for irem, ldiv, lrem, array elements, fields and arraylength. (2) This repository's class path: JBMC's stub of a JDK exception class has no superclass, so 'catch (RuntimeException e)' misses an ArithmeticException or IllegalArgumentException. Both shapes also gave false proofs under strict with --engine jbmc: caught, with --throws 'java.lang.ArithmeticException when n == 0', was proved, while the JVM returns -1.

JBMC's preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs) now finds both shapes in the bytecode JBMC reaches, as return-past-handler and stubbed-handler defects. A JBMC proof that reaches one is no verdict under every gap mode. A counterexample is still replayed, and prove's message names the defect when it doesn't reproduce. Tests: a unit test over 8 shapes in tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/p/D.java (4 defects, 4 neighbours JBMC runs as the JVM does), which fails with the detection disabled, and one for hold. End to end on the real JBMC, both false proofs are now refused (under assume too), caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 are unverifiable naming the defect, and exactCatch is still a violation. The corpus gains caught/3 and caughtAsRuntime/1 and /2 (lib/benchmark/conformance.json regenerated); they agree with the JVM on the own checker, and the inline test fails only on its 12 known JDK 25.0.5 disagreements. The lib unit tests (157), the other conformance tests and test_run.py pass. A report for cause 1 is drafted in the fixture's README for the user, not filed. The fix for cause 2, models of the exception hierarchy, belongs in lib/models and is recorded for the reconcile loop.

Job 20261106-203452 runs what needs JBMC: the integration tests, and the ignored conformance tests under jbmc, auto and auto --confirm.

Shared files changed, added to: lib/src/property.rs (the replay message asks the preflight first), lib/tests/conformance.rs and Conformance.java (three claims, one method), lib/README.md (a paragraph).

commits.summary: The 41 recorded JBMC examples run under strict on both engines, tabulated per obligation (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 4a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md, in the engines-jbmc stream. Job 20261106-204220 runs build.py on the 41 recorded B9/B11 examples JBMC proves (Quorum, Crosscut, Mica) in two scratch copies of examples/: as recorded (--engine jbmc, --gaps strict), and with only approach.engine set to native. It saves examples/tools/gap_table.py --json for each engine, every result.json, both build logs, and a comparison of the two tables. This replaces job 20261106-082917's projection, made under assume and rebuilt by hand, with a measured table. Recorded verdicts don't change: a verdict that differs from its expected one is reported in the table, not counted as a failure, and nothing in examples/ is written.

gap_table.py's rows now name their engine and checker, the example's expectation, and, for an obligation with no verdict, its problem and whether it is a JBMC proof refused at a construct JBMC runs otherwise than the JVM. That is step 3's guard, which records the defect only in the problem text. The summary counts the obligations with no verdict at a gap (under strict, a refused proof is already unresolved), those refused at a JBMC defect, and the examples that differ from their expected verdict. --compare lists the obligations whose status differs between two tables, the input to step 4c's coverage inventory.

commits.summary: JBMC right-shifts by the whole distance: the preflight names an unmasked shift and refuses a JBMC proof through one
commits.body:
Found while reading step 2b's benchmark job 20261106-201041 (passed) for 2c: the one case whose class differed between JBMC's staging policies, conformance/shiftRight/2, has a counterexample under full-range and tight (x = -2147483648, s = 33) that does not reproduce. JBMC 6.11.0 masks the distance of the left shifts (--show-goto-functions: shl(x, bitand(s, 31))) but not of the right ones (ashr(x, s), lshr), for int and long, so a distance outside 0..31 (0..63) fills the value with its sign or zeros where the JVM shifts by the distance's low bits. It also gave false proofs under strict: x >> s where s == 33, asserting result == 0 || result == -1, was verified by JBMC under both policies, while the JVM gives shiftRight(4, 33) == 2; likewise x >>> s == 0 where s == 32. The own checker refutes both.

lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs gains a third Defect, unmasked-shift: a right shift whose distance is not a constant within the width, nor its bitwise and with one, computed by instructions no branch joins. As with step 3's two, a JBMC proof that reaches one is refused under every --gaps mode and a counterexample is still replayed, its message naming the defect. The rule is broad (conformance/shiftRight/1, a correct JBMC proof under x == -1, is now refused; auto proves it on the own checker); constant distances are untouched. In the apps only Quorum's Backoff has a variable right shift, and its JBMC examples (016, 019) are violations.

Verified: the preflight's fixture test (renamed the_preflight_names_where_jbmc_runs_the_bytecode_otherwise_than_the_jvm) covers 3 new defects and 3 neighbours (s & 31, >> 1, <<) and fails with the detection disabled. The corpus gains conformance/shiftRight/3 and shiftUnsigned/3, the two false proofs, which agree with the JVM on the own checker; lib/benchmark/conformance.json is regenerated (98 claims). On the real JBMC both are now refused naming the defect, and auto gives the violation. Lib 157, integration 63, skill, test_run.py and test_gap_table.py pass; conformance fails only on its 12 known JDK 25.0.5 disagreements. A draft upstream report for this cause is in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/README.md, its reproducer checked on JBMC and the JVM; not filed.

Shared files changed, added to: lib/tests/conformance.rs (two claims and a call), lib/README.md (a sentence). Progress also records the three collected jobs: -201041 passed (2c next); -203452 failed in its integration step (a JBMC timeout on Pricing#total) and under auto --confirm; -204220 (4a) failed because the examples' result schema does not allow 1b's stated.checker.sat, to fix and resubmit.

commits.summary: JBMC searches the full range alone by default, on benchmark job 20261106-201041's evidence
commits.body:
Step 2c of engine-priorities.md. Job 20261106-201041 ran the corpus under JBMC's three staging policies. Under strict, JBMC's proofs were the same 54 of 65 under each, in 654 s under staged, 575 s under full-range and 588 s under tight; the hard ones took half the time without the stages (bounded binary search 26 s against 56 s, example 141 31 s against 61 s). Counterexamples took 9 s against 27 s, no shrunk witness was larger, and no run under full-range was starved. Under auto the policies gave the same verdicts. The one case whose class changed, conformance/shiftRight/2, is JBMC's unmasked right shift (the previous commit), which staged's witness happened to miss; it is not a worse verdict of the policy, and is now the one case where --engine jbmc answers unverifiable where it gave a violation (the own checker and auto decide it).

So full-range is now the default of --jbmc-staging on prove and equivalence, of Options::new in property.rs and equivalence.rs, and of lib/benchmark/run.py. deadline.rs's module comment records the evidence. The own checker keeps its stages, as decided, and --confirm already ran the full range. lib/README.md and lib/benchmark/README.md describe the new default with the job's figures.

commits.summary: Under --confirm, a JBMC refutation through a named defect, whose witness does not reproduce, is no verdict; job 20261106-203452 triaged (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-203452 (step 3 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md) failed two of its three steps. Its --confirm step had 12 disagreements, all on conformance/caught, caughtAsRuntime and nestedHandler under strict and assume: the own checker proves the claim, and JBMC's confirming run refutes it at n = 0 through return-past-handler or stubbed-handler, the defects step 3 found and guards against, on a witness the interpreter does not reproduce. The tool called that a disagreement. Now equivalence::confirm runs JBMC's preflight on a refutation too, and takes the caller's replay of the witness in the harness: when the preflight names a defect and the witness does not reproduce, the refutation is the defect's, as a JBMC proof through one is refused, so the confirmation is no-verdict and the own checker's proof stands, unconfirmed, the line naming the defects. A witness that reproduces is still a disagreement, as is one with no defect in reach.

Its integration step failed at the own checker's regression proof of fixtures.Pricing#total in the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs, not at JBMC as the brief's Progress had said. Inline on cvm, 2 of 8 identical runs ran out of 40 s where the others took 4 s: the own checker's branch probes are budgeted by wall-clock time, so its path order depends on timing. That is lib/src/bmc/, the native stream's, so it is recorded under Progress with a reproducer for the native stream and the reconcile loop, and nothing there changed. That step's tee also failed, since lib/target did not exist yet in the job's fresh checkout.

Verified: on the real JBMC (milliseconds), caught, caughtAsRuntime and nestedHandler under auto --confirm are now verified, not confirmed, naming the defect. A new test, confirm_takes_a_refutation_through_a_jbmc_defect_for_no_verdict, uses a stand-in JBMC whose program reaches caught, for prove and equivalence, and fails with the fix disabled. Lib 157 tests and the conformance tests pass, except the corpus's 12 known disagreements from the contract records (JDK 25.0.5 against 25.0.4.1). lib/README.md's --confirm paragraph says so. Shared files changed: lib/tests/conformance.rs (fake_jbmc reads an optional goto.txt; the test), equivalence.rs and property.rs (confirm's closure and its two calls), lib/README.md.

Job 20261106-231317 reruns the three steps, with lib/target created first. The corpus under JBMC and auto also hasn't run since the unmasked-shift claims and the full-range default went in.

commits.summary: The examples' result schema allows the statement's SAT solver record; 4a's job rerun (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-204220, step 4a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md (the 41 recorded JBMC examples under strict on both engines), stopped in both engine steps at its first example: build.py refused 013's result against examples/schema/result.schema.json because 'sat' was unexpected. That is step 1b's stated.checker.sat, the SAT solver each result's evidence now names, which the schema did not allow yet. The checker object in the statement now allows sat, in the shape lib/src/statement.rs Sat serializes (solver, version or null, source, configuration), and nothing more.

Verified inline: real sat records from a millisecond proof on each engine, spliced into the 14 committed results that carry a statement, pass build.py's whole validation (flat schema, round trip through the stored format, stored schema), and a record with an extra field is refused; three real statements (own checker, JBMC, auto --confirm) validate in full against $defs/statement; test_build.py has the same 35 pre-existing errors before and after the change, and test_gap_table.py passes.

Job 20261106-231837 reruns -204220's three steps unchanged at this commit, so it also measures the unmasked-shift guard, --confirm's rule for refutations through a defect, and the full-range default on the examples. The stream's status is now waiting on jobs 20261106-231317 and 20261106-231837.

commits.summary: The examples' result schema allows a run's phasesExcess; 3's rerun passed, 4a's JBMC table measured, its own-checker step rerun (verification pending)
commits.body:
Job 20261106-231317, the rerun of step 3's job (llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md), passed: 63 integration tests, the corpus under jbmc and auto (98 claims, 196 runs, the unmasked-shift claims and the full-range default included) and under auto --confirm, where the 12 disagreements of -203452 are gone. Phase 3 is done: the cause of the witnesses that don't reproduce is known, guarded with tests, and drafted as reports for the user.

Job 20261106-231837, step 4a's rerun, measured JBMC's per-obligation table under strict over the 41 recorded JBMC examples: 43 obligations, 27 refuted, 13 established, 3 unresolved. 071#0 and #1 are no verdict at the Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf stubs, as job -082917 projected. 037#0, the one example that differs from its expected verdict, is a JBMC proof refused by the unmasked-shift guard at -1 >>> Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(cap - 1), whose distance is 32 when cap == 1. Checked inline on the JVM over all 2^32 ints: the recorded proof is correct, since JBMC's wrong value for that shift gives the same result there, so the refusal is the guard's breadth, recorded for 037's notes and 4c.

Its own-checker step stopped at example 018: build.py refused the result because the schema's search.runs items did not allow phasesExcess, step 1a's flag on a run whose named phases add up past its seconds. Reproduced inline: the own checker's 0.18 s run of 018 has sampled encoding (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs ENCODING_SAMPLE) and solving 0.013 s past it beyond the tolerance, recorded for the native stream. Each run in examples/schema/result.schema.json may now carry phasesExcess, a positive number. Verified: that real run record, spliced into the 14 committed results with runs, passes build.py's whole check_result validation; negative and string values are refused (42 of 42 as expected); the schema at the previous commit refuses the real record; the run's full search record validates; test_build.py has the same 35 pre-existing errors and test_gap_table.py passes.

Job 20261107-000039 reruns -231837's three steps unchanged at this commit, so the own checker's table and the comparison come from one commit. The stream's status is now waiting on it.

commits.summary: 4a's job 20261107-000039 passed: both engines' strict tables over the 41 JBMC examples, and their comparison; the stream's phases are done
commits.body: Job 20261107-000039, step 4a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md, passed (4 m 22 s, peak 1.1 GiB). It ran build.py on the 41 recorded B9/B11 JBMC examples under --gaps strict on each engine, in scratch copies, and saved gap_table.py --json for each. JBMC's table is row for row the one job -231837 measured: of 43 obligations, 27 refuted, 13 established, 3 unresolved (071#0 and #1 at the Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf stubs; 037#0 a correct proof refused by the unmasked-shift guard). The own checker's: 24 refuted, 11 established, 8 unresolved, at Quorum's TermOrder.<clinit> (013#0, 071#0-#2), at Integer/Long.numberOfLeadingZeros, which strict refuses (037#0, 127#0), at a float parameter (035#0) and at --unwind 16 (052#0). The engines agree on all 35 obligations both decide; JBMC alone decides 5 (013#0, 035#0, 052#0, 071#2, 127#0), the own checker alone none, and neither 3. Recorded verdicts are unchanged; the differences are reported for the reconcile loop's 4c, which takes the tables as they stand from the default workspace's lib/target/jobs/4a-coverage/.
The engines-jbmc stream's last turns, recorded by the reconcile loop of engine-priorities.md before the merge, so its conversation follows its last commit on its branch. No code changed.
